title: kbmon's sprint estimate is a range from per-kind history that keeps moving while an item runs
goal: kbmon.py --status sprints gives an active sprint's time left as a range with its basis and a confidence word, from the claim-to-done times of recent items of the same kind plus the sprint's review, retrospective and close tail, not from the gaps between done commits; an item in progress counts its kind's estimate less its elapsed time, never below a floor, or its landing step while it lands, so a planted long item in progress neither freezes nor inflates the estimate; items that may run side by side within the worker limit are counted in parallel, items that depend on each other or share touches one after another; the live view's sprint panel and kb_monitor_status show the same estimate from the same function; kbmon.py --status sprints --backtest N replays the estimator over the last N closed sprints at 25, 50 and 75 percent of each and prints its median absolute error, its median relative error and the share of actual close times inside the range; the target, not yet backed by data for the new estimator, is a median relative error of at most 35 percent over the last 20 closed sprints, where the commit-gap estimate measures 51 percent on the same points, with at least half of the close times inside the range

gates.question: Approve this sprint's goal and committed items?
